title: House Could Vote Next Week on Impeaching Hegseth as Republicans Blame Pentagon Chief for Iran War
dek: Rep. Thomas Massie says he will force an impeachment vote when Congress returns. Multiple Republican sources told CNN they expect it to pass.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, told CNN he plans to trigger a House vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Congress returns next week.
Multiple Republican sources told CNN they expect the impeachment measure to pass, according to CNN.
Massie filed eight impeachment accusations against Hegseth in September, Al Jazeera reported, and lost his May primary, leaving him only the current session to pursue the effort.
Trump told reporters on Wednesday he was not considering replacing Hegseth and said, "I think he is doing a very good job," Al Jazeera reported.
body:
The House of Representatives could vote as soon as next week on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, weeks before the Democratic majority is sworn in, CNN reported. The possible vote follows Republican losses in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

## Republicans point to the Iran war

Some Republicans want to blame Hegseth for persuading President Donald Trump to attack Iran with no exit strategy, CNN reported. Republican strategists privately acknowledged that the party's problems extend beyond the war, CNN said, noting that Trump is commander in chief and that the decision to attack was his. Vice President JD Vance wrote on X, "The reason we lost is the war," and Trump told reporters the war had affected the results.

## Massie's case

Massie told CNN that he plans to trigger the vote when Congress returns. Al Jazeera quoted him saying Hegseth is "abusing the power of his office to ignore congressional war powers resolutions" and to "intimidate critics of the Trump administration." Massie has also called on Hegseth to resign, Al Jazeera reported.

## Trump's position

Trump said he was not considering replacing Hegseth. White House insiders told CNN that Trump supports Hegseth and wants him to fight against impeachment. CNN also reported that many Republican lawmakers remain reluctant to break from Trump.

## What is not yet known

Reporting reviewed for this story does not establish how many House votes an impeachment measure would have, and it does not say when the vote will be held. Any House impeachment would go to a Senate that remains controlled by Republicans until the new Congress takes office in January, Al Jazeera reported. Meridian will update this story when a vote is scheduled or held.

## Who decides

Hegseth's fate would be decided by a Congress still dominated by Republicans, with the Democrats who won this week taking office in January, Al Jazeera reported. Some reports suggest Republican lawmakers are increasingly inclined to push Hegseth out of the Pentagon, Al Jazeera said.

Al Jazeera also reported that Massie lost his Republican House primary in May to a challenger backed by the president. Massie has long been at odds with Trump, and has criticized the Iran war and the administration's military support for Israel, Al Jazeera reported. He has also voted against Trump's signature tax legislation, according to the same report.

## Context from the campaign

Some Republican lawmakers and critics have argued that Hegseth played a leading role in persuading Trump to attack Iran without an exit strategy, CNN and Al Jazeera reported. Many Republicans, however, remain unwilling to blame Trump directly, even as they recognize the Iran war as a main reason for the midterm losses, Al Jazeera said. Vance, while not assigning blame to any one person, said "the reason we lost is the war."

The Guardian reported on Nov. 4 that Hegseth may take the fall for the Republican midterm losses despite Trump's support. Trump, asked about Hegseth on Wednesday, said he was "doing a very good job," according to Al Jazeera.
